newsitem.title: USA: OM Group proceeds with Congo cobalt plant.
newsitem.headline: OM Group proceeds with Congo cobalt plant.

text.p: The OM Group said cobalt from its new Democratic Republic of Congo project signed this week will come on stream within two years.
Cleveland-based OM is taking a 51 percent stake in a smelter built in Lubumbashi to concentrate converter slag into cobalt-copper alloy at the rate of 5,000 tonnes a year of contained cobalt.
Formerly Zaire, Congo's state-owned mining company Gecamines and Entreprise General Malta Forrest Sprl own the remaining shares in the $80 million project of which OM will fund half.

OM's Chief Financial Officer Jim Materna said all the cobalt-copper alloy will be taken to the company's Kokkola refinery in Finland for further processing and used internally to make cobalt salts, chemicals and powders used in ceramics, catalysts, paintdriers and glassware.
Materna declined to say what the production costs of the plant will be.
All feasibility and engineering work for the smelter has been completed, and construction will begin in the second half of this year. The estimated life of the slag stockpile is 20 years.
"We expect to get product out from the beginning of 1999," Materna said.
In the meantime, OMG said it will be supplied with cobalt from concentrates from the Luiswishi mine, also in Congo.
